title: Transfer the δ halo exponents 11, 24, 26, 26, 6 across cells; robust to the 'rounded' reading (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds `research/delta-cross-cell-transfer/`. It answers the open question of #4452 (and of my #4460): do jwr404's within-cell δ exponents 11, 24, 26, 26 and 6 survive on the banded reference across cells?

**Claim type:** a conditional transfer lemma plus a robustness lemma, with exact rational checks. **No new κ.** The ideal gaps `1/(8p²)` stay hypotheses.

## Results

- **Lemma A (downward reading, LOG-A + #4449's `0 ≤ H ≤ n`).** This is #4442's column split with δ in place of `1/(16p²)`. It gives `off(H) ≤ T_in/(1−δ) + T_out ≤ (1−g)/(1−δ)`. The global inverse ceiling is therefore exactly #4452's `U`, and all five exponents transfer verbatim.
- **Lemma B (any reading with excess `ρ ≤ 1/(32p³)` per row or column).** We get `‖H^{−1}‖₂ < 10p²`, so 11, 24, 26, 26 and 6 all hold. Per entry, an absolute error up to `1/(64p⁴)` in either direction suffices.
- **What Lemma B changes.** #4442 found that under `16p²−1`, a 1/64 overshoot broke `p = 2`, so the downward-vs-"rounded" (FINE-PRIME) wording mattered. Under δ it no longer matters for these exponents. FINE-PRIME's `poly(p)2^{−(C−o(1))p}` perturbation works eventually.
- **Near-tightness.** At `p = 2` the excess tolerance on this route lies in `(0.0091, 0.0092)`.

## Evidence

```text
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/delta-cross-cell-transfer --check-only
  PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/delta-cross-cell-transfer
  PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/delta-cross-cell-transfer outcome=completed   (~45 s, stdlib only)
```

The checks are exact for each `p` from 2 to 64, plus all-`p` inequalities. The split identity is proved as a polynomial identity on a 3×3×3 grid. The LOG-A, FINE-PRIME and downstream phrases are pinned. Head: `c8fd7f81696d5b8b838c996cc384e76ab378dae3`. Base: canonical main `2a13eb18`.

## Not covered

- The ideal gaps.
- Page-generator implementation.
- The Schur complement and the core exponent 400.
- Any new κ.
